questions.questionText: The primary purpose of a religious initiation ceremony is to

options.text: Mark an important transition in life

questions.explanation: Rites of passage often mark movement from one stage of life to another.

questions.questionText: Which value is most directly promoted by caring for vulnerable family members?
questions.explanation: Care for vulnerable people expresses compassion and social responsibility.

questions.questionText: A family is best described as

options.text: Only people living in the same country
A social unit based on relationships and responsibilities
Any group of people in one classroom

questions.explanation: Families may take different forms but involve relationships and responsibilities.

questions.questionText: Which practice is most likely to strengthen family communication?
questions.explanation: Open discussion allows concerns and expectations to be shared.

questions.questionText: A religious text is often used by believers to
questions.explanation: Sacred texts commonly provide teachings and guidance for conduct.

questions.questionText: Which action best demonstrates forgiveness?

options.text: Choosing to release resentment after wrongdoing

questions.explanation: Forgiveness involves letting go of resentment and seeking restoration where appropriate.

questions.questionText: A major responsibility of parents or guardians is to
questions.explanation: Care and guidance are central responsibilities of parenting.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of responsible decision-making?

options.text: Choosing the fastest option regardless of harm

questions.explanation: Responsible decisions consider evidence, consequences and values.

questions.questionText: Religious diversity means

options.text: Different religions or beliefs exist within society

questions.explanation: Diversity recognizes the presence of different beliefs and practices.

questions.questionText: Which principle is most useful in resolving a family conflict?
questions.explanation: Respectful dialogue can identify concerns and support reconciliation.

questions.questionText: In Zimbabwean Indigenous Religion, what is the primary role of a mudzimu (ancestral spirit)?

options.text: To replace Mwari as Supreme Creator
To act as intermediary protecting the family and interceding with Mwari

questions.explanation: Ancestral spirits guard family morality and mediate between living descendants and Musikavanhu (Mwari).

questions.questionText: What is the traditional Shona ceremony held roughly a year after burial to bring the deceased parent's spirit back home to protect the family?
questions.explanation: Kurova guva (Umbuyiso in Ndebele) integrates the ancestor safely into the family homestead.

questions.questionText: Why is eating or marrying someone of the same totem (mutupo) traditionally taboo in Shona and Ndebele cultures?

options.text: It is forbidden only for chiefs
People sharing a totem are regarded as blood kin/siblings

questions.explanation: Shared totems signify common ancestry, preventing incest and preserving clan solidarity.

questions.questionText: In Judaism, which annual festival celebrates the liberation of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Pesach commemorates the Exodus from Egypt.

questions.questionText: Which covenant sign did God give to Abraham in Judaism?

options.text: Circumcision of male infants on the eighth day

questions.explanation: Circumcision (Brit Milah) marks the Abrahamic covenant in Genesis 17.

questions.questionText: What is the Bar Mitzvah ceremony in Judaism?

options.text: A coming-of-age ceremony when a 13-year-old boy becomes responsible for keeping Torah commandments

questions.explanation: At 13 (12 for girls: Bat Mitzvah), Jewish youth assume adult religious responsibility.

questions.questionText: In Christianity, what does the parable of the Good Samaritan primarily teach?

options.text: Show practical compassion and neighbourly love regardless of ethnic or religious barriers

questions.explanation: Jesus defined "neighbour" broadly across social/ethnic divisions through active mercy.

questions.questionText: Which Christian sacrament uses bread and wine (or grape juice) to commemorate Jesus' Last Supper?
questions.explanation: Eucharist / Lord's Supper recalls Christ's sacrifice.

questions.questionText: In Islam, what does "Zakat" require of financially able Muslims?

options.text: Giving a fixed annual proportion (~2.5%) of surplus wealth to the poor and needy

questions.explanation: Zakat is obligatory charitable almsgiving purifying wealth and assisting the poor.

questions.questionText: Which city do Muslims face during Salah (daily ritual prayers)?
questions.explanation: The Qibla directs prayer towards the Kaaba in Mecca.

questions.questionText: What is the core African philosophical ethic "Unhu / Ubuntu" best summarised as?

options.text: "I am because we are" — humanity expressed through mutual care, respect, and community solidarity

questions.explanation: Ubuntu/Unhu emphasises relational dignity, hospitality, honesty, and shared humanity.

questions.questionText: Under Zimbabwe's Constitution and religious teaching on child protection, child marriage (under age 18) is:

options.text: Legally prohibited and a violation of children's rights and dignity

questions.explanation: Zimbabwean law strictly prohibits marriage under 18 to protect education, health, and child rights.

questions.questionText: In Indigenous Religion, what is the purpose of "Chisi" (sacred rest day)?

options.text: To allow miners to blast rocks
To honour ancestral/territorial spirits, rest farmers/oxen, and promote ecological conservation

questions.explanation: Observing Chisi ensures communal rest and respect for Mwari and land guardian spirits (mhondoro).

questions.questionText: Which sacred scripture is believed by Muslims to be the final literal revelation of Allah given to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is Islam's central revealed scripture.

questions.questionText: Which religious response is most constructive in addressing HIV and AIDS in Zimbabwean communities?

options.text: Providing compassionate home-based care, accurate testing/ART encouragement, and moral support

questions.explanation: Faith communities play a vital role fighting stigma and supporting holistic care alongside medical treatment.

questions.questionText: What does "monotheism" mean?

options.text: Belief in and worship of one Supreme God

questions.explanation: Judaism, Christianity, Islam, and Indigenous belief in Mwari affirm one Supreme Creator.

questions.questionText: In traditional Shona courtship, what is the symbolic role of "roora/lobola" when practised responsibly?

options.text: Covenant token of appreciation uniting two families and thanking the bride's parents
A fine paid to the village head

questions.explanation: Traditionally, roora cements kinship bonds between two families—not commercial sale.

questions.questionText: Which Old Testament figure is honoured across Judaism, Christianity, and Islam as a model of faith and obedience?
questions.explanation: All three Abrahamic faiths trace spiritual heritage to Abraham.

questions.questionText: In environmental stewardship across world religions, how should humans treat forests, water, and wildlife?

options.text: Exploit them recklessly for short-term profit
Act as responsible caretakers/stewards preserving creation for future generations

questions.explanation: Sacred groves/totems in ATR and stewardship teachings in Bible/Qur'an command careful conservation.

questions.questionText: How does interfaith dialogue strengthen national cohesion in a pluralistic Zimbabwe?

options.text: By building mutual respect, dispelling prejudice, and uniting faiths on charity and peacebuilding
By forcing everyone into one denomination

questions.explanation: Interfaith dialogue fosters peace and shared civic action across denominations.

questions.questionText: What is "Sawm" in the Five Pillars of Islam?

options.text: Fasting from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan

questions.explanation: Sawm builds self-discipline, spiritual devotion, and empathy for the hungry.

questions.questionText: Which Christian Beatitude promises blessing to "the peacemakers"?

options.text: They shall be called children of God

questions.explanation: Matthew 5:9 — "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God."

questions.questionText: In Zimbabwean Indigenous Religion, "Mhondoro" are:

options.text: Senior territorial/royal spirits guarding whole chieftaincies, rainfall, and land fertility

questions.explanation: Mhondoro spirits oversee rainfall (mukwerera), chieftaincy legitimacy, and communal wellbeing.

questions.questionText: Why do religious teachings discourage corruption and bribery in public institutions?

options.text: Because corruption violates honesty, justice, and harms the poor and vulnerable
Because only private firms face ethics

questions.explanation: All major faiths demand fairness, accountability, and protection of the powerless.

questions.questionText: In Judaism, the weekly day of rest and worship observed from Friday sunset to Saturday nightfall is called:
questions.explanation: Shabbat commemorates creation rest and liberation from bondage.
